plan.title: Liver drug treatment DE (3v3) with power caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq from human liver tissue, 3 drug-treated vs 3 control samples, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples used for DE; a 7th column in counts.csv beyond the 6-sample metadata is checked and excluded if it is an extra unannotated sample). Since counts already are gene-level integer counts (not transcript-level Salmon quant files), the tximport/length-offset step from the knowledge base does not apply here — the plan proceeds directly from the gene x sample count matrix, which is the standard entry point for DESeq2. The flow follows the knowledge-grounded procedure for a 3-vs-3 fixed-effects design: (1) sample-structure QC via blind VST, PCA and sample-distance heatmap to check the samples cluster by condition and to catch any outlier before modeling; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size); (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization built into the model; (4) an explicit factor with control set as the reference level and the contrast named condition treated_vs_control; (5) the DESeq2 Wald test as the primary DE test, cross-checked with an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and design, reporting the intersection as the high-confidence gene set per the robustness rule for low-replicate designs; (6) apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2 fold change for ranking and plotting; (7) BH FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and a pre-adjustment p-value histogram to check the test's null behavior; (8) fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1, staged locally) then Reactome (staged locally) as the follow-up collection, since an ORA on a short significant gene list would be underpowered at n=3; (9) an integrated report that states the expected statistical power at n=3 per group explicitly — count-based DE tools at this replicate number recover only a minority of true differentially expressed genes, biased toward large fold changes, so a gene absent from the significant list is not evidence of no effect. All diagnostic and threshold choices (10 read minimum filter, alpha 0.05, apeglm shrinkage, BH correction, Hallmark-then-Reactome enrichment order, stat as the GSEA ranking metric) follow the grounded procedure returned by the knowledge service for this exact situation (bulk RNA-seq, human, 2 groups, n=3 per group, unpaired, single batch, Salmon-derived counts).
